title: Empirical Interflow Response and Singular-Tangent Policy

physics_scope.contribution_only: interflow drainage-side contribution, not the complete DRAMET=3 level exchange
physics_scope.inactive_contribution: q = 0 for difference < 0; negative-side infiltration belongs outside this candidate

data_separation.legacy_owltab_date_parsing: adapter/runtime concern, excluded from process kernel

derivative_contract.exact_activation: full derivative unavailable because activation is a branch boundary
derivative_contract.activation_for_exponent_eq_1: right-hand drainage tangent is finite and equals coefficient, but full two-sided derivative remains unavailable
derivative_contract.near_activation: return exact finite analytic tangent whenever representable; no process-side smoothing, cap, tolerance or hidden threshold
derivative_contract.unrepresentable_tangent: fail closed as numerical domain, never publish infinity/NaN as usable derivative
derivative_contract.solver_ownership: solver/numerical policy decides whether and how to consume a finite process tangent and owns any bounded-cost fallback

mass_and_transaction_contract.sign: positive q is water leaving soil toward drainage receiver
mass_and_transaction_contract.mass_role: response is an authoritative proposed external-transfer contribution; accepted ledger booking remains runtime-owned
mass_and_transaction_contract.rejected_trials: must never alter committed state or committed ledger

hard_holds: No negative-side infiltration/reverse exchange implementation in F-PM08C3.
No DIVDRA or spatial distribution implementation.
No multi-level aggregation; that remains F-PM08C4.
No surface-water storage/control; that remains F-PM08D.
No solver Jacobian mutation and no HeadCalc internals in process code.
No process-side tangent smoothing, clipping, epsilon activation band or configurable mass tolerance.
No runtime or canonical admission claim in this structural/scientific candidate workunit.
required_tests: legacy flux identity across coefficient/exponent bounds and positive activation differences spanning multiple scales
analytic derivative versus independent finite difference away from activation
inactive contribution q=0 and derivative=0 below activation
exact activation q=0 with derivative unavailable
finite drainage-side activation diagnostic for exponent=1 without claiming a full derivative
nonfinite and out-of-domain inputs fail closed
no persistent process state or I/O/HeadCalc leakage
